cards.title: Introduction to Authentication
cards.content:
Authentication is the process of verifying who a user is, while authorization is verifying what they have access to.

In a Vue.js single-page application (SPA), we typically use token-based authentication, such as JSON Web Tokens (JWT), interacting with a backend API.

items.text: User submits login credentials (username/password) via a Vue form.
Backend validates credentials and generates a JWT.
Vue app receives and stores the token in localStorage or cookies.
Vue app includes the token in the Authorization header for subsequent API requests.

cards.title: Managing Auth State with Pinia
cards.content:
Pinia is the official state management library for Vue.js. Here is how you can structure an auth store:

import { defineStore } from 'pinia';
import { ref } from 'vue';

export const useAuthStore = defineStore('auth', () => {
  const token = ref(localStorage.getItem('token') || null);
  const isAuthenticated = computed(() => !!token.value);

  function setToken(newToken) {
    token.value = newToken;
    localStorage.setItem('token', newToken);
  }

  return { token, isAuthenticated, setToken };
});

cards.title: Securing Routes with Navigation Guards
cards.content:
Vue Router allows us to protect routes using navigation guards. We can check if a user is authenticated before allowing access to a view.

router.beforeEach((to, from, next) => {
  const authStore = useAuthStore();
  if (to.meta.requiresAuth && !authStore.isAuthenticated) {
    next('/login');
  } else {
    next();
  }
});
